marks.gloss_en: השתא דאמרת צדדין אסורין -- Rav Ashi applies the ruling to the ladder
Rav Ashi: this raised ladder -- a person should not lean it on the palm tree, but on stakes outside the palm; and when he climbs he should not put his foot on the stakes but on the rungs
הכא בכלכלה דחוקה עסקינן... וקמשתמש באילן גופיה (= p_kalkala_dechuka)
Rav Pappa: here we deal with a tight basket, so that as he takes the eruv he moves the tree, and uses the tree itself
the baraita: if he drove a stake into a tree and hung a basket on it [with his eruv], above ten handbreadths his eruv is no eruv; below ten handbreadths his eruv is an eruv
one may untie bundles of sheaves before an animal
היכי משכחת לה? -- how could hay be too hard [for an animal] to eat?
אמר לך רב הונא: לא, שחת דומיא דחרובין -- the hay is like the carobs, hard; crushing it is rendering food, not exertion (= p_huna_shachat_akusha)
no: the hay is like the carobs -- as the carobs are hard, so the hay is hard

תא שמע: רבי יהודה מתיר בחרובין לדקה -- לדקה אין, לגסה לא. If the tanna kamma forbids exertion and permits rendering food, R' Yehuda's 'for the small' is also rendering food; but if the tanna kamma forbids rendering food and permits exertion, R' Yehuda who permits for the small should כל שכן permit for the large
מי סברת דקה -- דקה ממש? daka is a large animal particular about its food (= p_daka_dayka; pressed by the kashya at 155a.12)
what is daka? a large animal; and why call it daka? because it is particular (dayka) about its food
Rav Yehuda: peki'in and zirin are the same [kind of bundle]; zirin are of three
one may chop pumpkins before an animal and a carcass before dogs
